# k0rdent_service_account (Data Source)

One service account, read rather than managed.

Use it to hand a pipeline's `client_id` to the configuration that needs it, or to check the account is still `active`, without putting its destroy in this state file. Like the resource, it takes no `region` and no `project`, and is addressed inside an organization. Unlike a project's, the organization can't be looked up from the id: the platform lists service accounts only within a scope.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A service account another configuration owns. Fails the plan if it isn't
# active.

data "k0rdent_service_account" "deployer" {
  organization_id = "org-ml-platform"
  id              = "sa-ml-platform-deployer"

  lifecycle {
    postcondition {
      condition     = self.status == "active"
      error_message = "${self.id} is ${self.status}, so nothing can authenticate as it."
    }
  }
}

output "deployer_client_id" {
  value = data.k0rdent_service_account.deployer.client_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Service account id. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL. String length must be at most 63.
- `organization_id` (String) The organization the service account is in. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL. String length must be at most 63.

### Read-Only

- `active_credential_count` (Number) Credentials that haven't expired, of the five an account can hold. It drops on its own as credentials lapse.
- `client_id` (String) The OAuth2 client id the account authenticates with.
- `created_at` (String) When it was created, as RFC 3339.
- `created_by` (String) The user id of the administrator who created it.
- `description` (String) What the account is for, if anyone said.
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name the account is shown under.
- `roles` (Set of String) Role slugs bound to the account at its scope.
- `scope` (String) The level its roles apply at: `organization`, `folder` or `project`.
- `scope_id` (String) The organization, folder or project `scope` names.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this service account.
- `status` (String) `active`, or `disabled`, in which case no credential of it mints a token and its outstanding tokens were revoked when it was disabled.
- `updated_at` (String) When it last changed, as RFC 3339.
